meta.title: XR Training Launcher
meta.subtitle: Pitt-Bradford XR training examples. Pick a tile to launch it.

sections.title: Browser demos
sections.intro: Run in any WebGL browser on this PC. Each has a desktop fallback; the ENTER VR button appears only where the browser and headset support WebXR.

sections.title: Multiplayer (needs the relay)
sections.intro: These pages talk to the WebSocket relay. Open this launcher from the relay (port 8443) so the links reach it.

sections.title: Vive / SteamVR (Unity)
sections.intro: Unity projects. They are not served by the web server; they run in the Unity editor on the Vive PC. The tiles open the project notes.

sections.title: Quest
sections.intro: Opened from the Quest Browser, using the controller pointer. Nothing here has been tested on a physical Quest yet.

demoPath.title: Frame the session
demoPath.what: Say these are learning prototypes, not certified training. Show this launcher and the badges that mark what is tested.

demoPath.title: Fieldwork Practice Lab on the desktop
demoPath.what: Open the lab, enter a name, and run one hands-on scenario such as Work at height. Point out the consequences and the critical safety misses.

demoPath.title: Same lab in a headset
demoPath.who: Volunteer in a headset; presenter on the desktop
demoPath.what: Volunteer presses ENTER VR and selects hotspots with a controller. Hardware test is still pending, so keep the desktop view ready.

demoPath.title: Circuit Lab, shared bench
demoPath.who: Presenter on desktop, volunteer joins the same room
demoPath.what: Both join one room, load the demo circuit, close the switch, and watch the bulb light for everyone. Needs the relay.

demoPath.title: Site Safety Layout
demoPath.what: Load the sample layout and let the checklist call out the missing exit or barrier. Desktop fallback; AR needs a phone or headset with WebXR.

demoPath.title: Hydrostatic Test Bay in Unity
demoPath.what: Show the Unity scene in desktop mode and explain where the Vive work is heading. Not yet tested in a headset.

examples.title: Fieldwork XR Practice Lab
examples.summary: Seventeen hands-on practice scenarios with consequences, feedback and a score.

examples.summary: A faceted animated prism with orbiting lights, orbit controls and a VR entry button.

examples.title: Babylon.js Luminous Totem
examples.summary: A glowing totem with halo and beacons using Babylon's built-in WebXR experience.

examples.title: WebXR Color Field
examples.summary: Framework-free WebXR Device API sample: a desktop preview and a color-changing immersive session.

examples.title: Circuit Lab (multiplayer VR)
examples.summary: A shared electronics bench: snap together batteries, switches, bulbs and motors with others in one room.

examples.title: Site Safety Layout (multiplayer AR)
examples.summary: Plan exits, extinguishers and barriers together; a live checklist flags what is missing.
